answer: To make Sybil identities expensive, an agent market can require a nontransferable credential earned through random cross-domain verification. One applicant validates a weather sensor on a knoll, another reconciles nebula telescope logs, and a third checks summit trail measurements. Independent data owners sign the observations, and false evidence burns a per-identity deposit. Running a thousand counterfeit agents therefore requires a thousand real audits or risks a thousand lost deposits.
